datasets: Part 1 Crime Data (CSV) - declared, not shipped
311 Customer Service Requests (CSV) - declared, not shipped
concurrency_primitives: goroutine per dataset returning result channel (main.go:22-30); per-dataset worker pool of N parser goroutines over bounded jobs channel (ingest.go:71-91); sync.WaitGroup closes results (ingest.go:92); reader goroutine streams batches (ingest.go:95-116); per-worker private Agg merged by one goroutine (ingest.go:118-121, model.go:72-91)
design_patterns: Pipeline (Ingest reader->workers->merge), Strategy (Dataset interface, Question interface), Factory (NewCrimeDataset/New311Dataset)
questions: Mayor's Office: Which neighborhoods carry the most crime, and what does their 311 picture look like?
Public Works: Where is crime high but 311 engagement low (possible service gap / under-reporting)?
City Planning: Do neighborhoods with more crime also generate more 311 requests? (Pearson r, quartiles)
Transportation/DPW: Which 311 request types are over-represented in the highest-crime neighborhoods? (lift)
Operations: When do crime and 311 demand peak (by month and time of day)?
overview: Single-package Go CLI with a clean reader->bounded-channel->worker-pool->merge pipeline, table-driven Dataset strategies with header aliases, and a Question strategy interface for five analyses rendered as ASCII tables/bars. Code is concise, well commented, consistent with its README, race-clean and covered by three ingestion tests. Memory design (streaming, confinement, O(groups) aggregates, MemStats) is explicit and verified.
stakeholder_value: The question set (hotspots with 311 context, service-gap ratio, correlation, request-type lift, timing) is well framed and would be actionable on real data; report_real_data.txt hints at real findings (Inner Harbor under-reporting, curb-repair lift). But the submitted run uses uniformly random synthetic data, so every printed finding is an artefact (r=0.992, flat seasonality) and a stakeholder learns nothing from the shipped artefact.
issues: No real Open Baltimore data in the submission; only scripts/gen_sample.py output (Location='X', District='CENTRAL', 20 neighborhoods).
Synthetic sample files are the default -crime/-requests paths (rubric deduction).
report_real_data.txt asserts real-data results but cannot be reproduced from the submission; program has no download step.
Everything in one package; question logic has no tests.
Crime (2024) and 311 (2025) cover different years (acknowledged); counts not per-capita.
rationale: Full marks for build, memory design and README, near-full for concurrency and stakeholder framing, reflecting a well-engineered pipeline that builds, tests and runs race-free first try. The real_data criterion scores 2/15 because only generator output is present and it is the default path, and runs_results is reduced to 7 because the end-to-end run only ever processes synthetic data. Total 77 (C).
